# sealed recipient

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:sealedRecipient`](gmeow-sealedRecipient.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/sealedRecipient>
- **Category:** property
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/gts`](../../slices/gts.md)
- **Box roles:** [RBox role](../boxes/rbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

An agent for whom a sealed (encrypted) opaque frame is decryptable — the frame's declared audience (spec §9.3 recipients). Non-functional: a frame may be sealed to several recipients. The vantage-relativity of opacity made explicit: for these agents the frame is not opaque at all.

## Structure

**Property shape:** object property; [`gmeow:OpaqueFrame`](../classes/gmeow-OpaqueFrame.md) -> [`gmeow:Agent`](../classes/gmeow-Agent.md)

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:sealedRecipient`](gmeow-sealedRecipient.md) from [`gmeow:OpaqueFrame`](../classes/gmeow-OpaqueFrame.md) to [`gmeow:Agent`](../classes/gmeow-Agent.md) when the relationship itself belongs in the native GMEOW graph.

## Common Companion Terms

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use on a sealed (encrypt-class) opaque frame to name the agents who hold a key and can decrypt it — making explicit that opacity is vantage-relative and the frame is transparent to them.

### Avoid when

- Avoid for frames opaque through an unknown codec or damage (no recipient resolves those) and avoid treating it as an access-control grant; it describes who can decode, not a privacy-disclosure decision (that is the kernel sensitivity/disclosure axes).

### How to use

- List one or more [`gmeow:Agent`](../classes/gmeow-Agent.md) recipients on a frame whose [`gmeow:opacityReason`](gmeow-opacityReason.md) is [`gmeow:opacityMissingKey`](../individuals/gmeow-opacityMissingKey.md); the same frame stays opaque to every reader not on the list.

### Examples

- ex:frame7 [`gmeow:sealedRecipient`](gmeow-sealedRecipient.md) ex:lillith, ex:auditor.
